open_points.subject: context — M01 Project alias
open_points.text: its alias, a short neutral label the owner may give, the name the agent sees (R0-82); at most 40 characters (R0-90; Open questions);
open_points.question: Must the Project alias meaning also state R0-96's rule that it never names a person's condition, health, disability, age or other need, while remaining a writer obligation that Registry does not inspect?
options: Add the R0-96 prohibition to the alias meaning and writer rule
Keep only the older neutral-label and R0-82 restrictions
open_points.default_guess: Add the R0-96 prohibition to the model meaning, without making it a Registry validation rule or prematurely changing the first-release manifest description.

witness.initial: An active project has no alias.
events: The owner considers assigning the alias "Wheelchair renovation", which is within 40 Unicode code points and contains no person's name or address.
outcomes: Under the stated State 1 wording, the alias can be treated as satisfying the writer rule.
Under R0-96, the writer must not use it because it names a person's condition or need; Registry itself would still accept it if submitted.
witness.observer: The owner choosing the alias and, if it is written, the agent and its AI provider.

open_points.subject: context — M03 Room name
open_points.text: its name, as its writer wrote it (R0-68);
open_points.question: Must the Room name meaning state R0-96's closed writer rule: name the room by purpose and, where needed, number or position, and never by a person or a person's condition, health, disability, age or other need?
options: Carry the complete R0-96 writer rule into M03
Retain only the older reference to R0-68
open_points.default_guess: Carry the complete R0-96 rule into M03 while stating that Registry performs no content check.

witness.initial: An active project exists and its agent session is allowed to add a room.
events: The agent proposes the room name "Bathroom for the wheelchair" through Kernel.
The exact write receives any approval R0-99 requires and reaches Registry.
outcomes: Following M03's older R0-68 reference alone, a writer may regard the name as permitted because it contains no person's name or address.
Following R0-96, the writer must not submit that name because it expresses a person's health or need, although Registry would not reject it by content.
witness.observer: The owner approving the write and, if written, the agent and its AI provider.

open_points.subject: context — list projects answer
open_points.text: Answers a caller reads; each is a projection of the models above, shaped in States 5 and 6, with the disclosure class of each output declared (R0-26). None is a model: none has facts of its own.
open_points.question: What model facts must the owner action 'list projects' read and return after R0-93—specifically, must it support including archived projects and must every item carry customer_ref so all projects naming a customer can be found?
options: Declare an owner project-list projection whose items include customer_ref and which can include archived projects
Leave the project-list projection unspecified for States 5 and 6 to infer
open_points.default_guess: Declare that the owner can list active and archived projects and that each item carries project_id and customer_ref at minimum for the R0-93 procedure.

witness.initial: Customer C is named by one active project and one archived project.
events: The owner handles C's data-subject request.
The owner invokes 'list projects' with archived projects included to find every project naming C.
outcomes: Items carry customer_ref, so both projects are found and subsequently read.
Items omit customer_ref or archived projects, so the owner cannot assemble the prescribed complete set from this action.
witness.observer: The owner answering the data-subject request.

open_points.subject: context — M09 AuditEntry outcome
open_points.text: the outcome (accepted; whether refused attempts are recorded is settled in State 2, round 28 P1);
open_points.question: Must M09 now close the outcome to accepted changes only and state that refused attempts create no AuditEntry, because R0-97 places first-release refusals nowhere and second-release refusal information in separate in-memory counters?
options: AuditEntry records accepted changes only; refusals never create one
State 2 may still choose to record refused attempts as AuditEntry outcomes
open_points.default_guess: AuditEntry records accepted changes only; refused attempts remain outside the audit log and, in the second release, affect only the separate counters.

witness.initial: Registry is running the first release and its audit log contains accepted changes.
events: A caller presents an unknown service token and Registry refuses the request.
The owner later opens the audit view.
outcomes: Under R0-97 and R0-100, no AuditEntry exists and the first release keeps no trace of the attempt.
If State 2 exercises the choice M09 still defers, an AuditEntry with a refused outcome may exist.
witness.observer: The owner reading the audit view.
